samples.summary: Fix is applied by mutating finding shape at the merge site rather than at the matcher layer that already knows the lens. `adjudicateRebuttals` (review-panel.mjs:1940) is already passed `lensId`, and `matchRebuttal` (rebuttal.mjs:183) synthesises its comparison operands inline — so `{ lens: finding?.lens ?? lensId, ... }`, or filtering `rebuttals` by `r.lens === lensId`, would fix the same inertness without adding a field to every persisted finding and without depending on which array the stamp lands on for identity preservation. The chosen layer works and is documented, but it makes correctness depend on a call-site ordering invariant (stamp `merged`, not `gatingRaw`) that any future refactor of the round loop can silently break, whereas the matcher-layer fix is invariant-free and also protects any other future caller of `matchRebuttal`.

The wiring test asserts on source text (`src.split("\n").filter((l) => /^\s*const merged =/.test(l))` plus a regex on the expression shape). It pins formatting rather than behaviour: renaming `merged`, wrapping the expression across lines, or moving the stamp one call earlier all fail the test without any behaviour change, and conversely it cannot detect a stamp with the wrong lens id at runtime. checks.test.mjs's workflow-invariant precedent is cited, but that asserts YAML config with no executable path; this asserts JS that a real integration seam (a thin exported per-lens round function) could cover directly.

The same rationale is now stated three times at near-identical length: the `stampLens` JSDoc (review-panel.mjs:780-810), the call-site comment (review-panel.mjs:2451-2479), and the design doc section (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1578+). The repo's convention is that the design doc carries the narrative and code comments carry the load-bearing constraint; ~75 lines of prose for a 4-line function will drift out of sync on the next change to this path.
